lean_scaffold:
-- IGProtocol scaffold: VINIT → FSPLIT → IMSCRIB → AFWD → FSPLIT → CLINK → EVALT → EVALF → FFUSE → AREV → ENGAGR → CLINK → FFUSE → IFIX → TANCH
-- (native ob3ect designer; elaborate against the kernel to verify)
name: the least vertex count forcing a monochromatic copy of

phase_0.boundary_condition: The existence of a finite Ramsey number for any two finite graphs, guaranteed by Ramsey's theorem.
phase_0.domain_name: the least vertex count forcing a monochromatic copy of
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.justification: Forward morphism from a candidate N to the full set of red/blue edge colorings of the complete graph on N vertices, the space that must be tested.

AREV.chosen_element: verdict return from coloring space to N arm
AREV.justification: Contravariant morphism that carries the fused verdict—sufficient, insufficient, or both—back to the arm representing the candidate N, completing the inner evaluation.

CLINK.chosen_element: composition of candidate N with its verdict
CLINK.justification: Sequential chaining that links the N arm's self-identity to the outcome of the coloring sweep, forming a single composed state for that candidate.

ENGAGR.justification: Dialetheia holder: the paraconsistent state where an N simultaneously forces and fails to force a monochromatic copy; kept live without explosion, structurally available even if classically unrealized.

EVALF.justification: Negative state on a coloring arm: this coloring avoids both G and H entirely, providing a constructive counterexample that proves N is insufficient.

EVALT.justification: Affirm state on a coloring arm: this coloring contains a red copy of G or a blue copy of H, so it does nothing to refute the sufficiency of the current N.

FFUSE.justification: Multiplication that rejoins all candidate arms by collecting those that registered true and selecting the smallest one; this resolves the open branches into the single Ramsey number.

FSPLIT.justification: Co-multiplication that opens the search: the single unknown Ramsey number bifurcates into arms, one for each positive integer N, to test whether N forces a monochromatic copy.

IFIX.justification: ROM fixation that appends the computed Ramsey number irrevocably to the formal corpus, preventing any later mutation of the result.

IMSCRIB.justification: Identity morphism that recognizes the current N as a self-contained candidate threshold, holding the number itself as an element on the arm.

TANCH.justification: The terminal anchor that contains the whole search, sealing the minimum sufficient N as the definitive output and closing the system.

VINIT.justification: Before any candidate is examined, the Ramsey number is absent from the register; the domain starts in a void where nothing is named.

phase_2.fuse_result: the minimum N whose arm carried a true verdict (all colorings force a monochromatic copy), i.e. the least vertex count forcing the event
phase_2.rejoin_note: Each arm inserts a nested split over its 2-colorings, evaluates every coloring with EVALT/EVALF, and fuses the coloring results into a single truth value for that N. The outer fuse then takes the minimum N where that inner fuse produced true; arms that produced false or both are discarded. Conflicting arms do not cancel—they are simply not minimum. The rejoin does NOT recreate the input set; it yields a single resolved number.
phase_2.split_input: the initial unknown Ramsey number, which must be some positive integer
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — a candidate N that is simultaneously proven sufficient and proven insufficient; a live contradiction held paraconsistently.
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) — a specific N is constructively refuted; there exists a 2-coloring of K_N that avoids both graphs.
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) — a specific N is constructively affirmed as sufficient; all colorings of K_N contain a red G or blue H.
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither sufficient nor insufficient: the Ramsey number has not been determined yet.

steps.domain_action: the Ramsey number is absent; the workspace is void
open the set of positive integers into distinct candidate arms N
on each arm, identify N as the current candidate threshold
for the given N, construct the complete graph K_N and generate every 2-coloring of its edges
within the N arm, branch over all generated colorings
compose the coloring with the property of containing a red G or blue H
this coloring forces a monochromatic copy — no counterexample here
this coloring avoids both G and H — a witness against sufficiency
fuse the coloring branches: if any arm brought EVALF, the N arm gets false; if all brought EVALT, it gets true; if both appear, it gets both
carry the fused verdict back from the coloring space to the N arm
for any N arm that arrives at both, hold the contradiction live without resolution
compose each N arm with its verdict into a single unit for collection
outer fuse — gather all N-with-verdict units, select the smallest N that carries true, and emit that number
write the resulting Ramsey number permanently into the Erdős corpus
seal the computation; the Ramsey number is fixed and the domain closes

phase_5.alfs_store: `Millennium/ErdosFormalize.lean` and its siblings, the canonical reference store of open Erdős statements and formal definitions
phase_5.compiler_frontend: Lean 4 proof assistant with the Millennium project build system, translating formal statements into kernel operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Kernel walk invoked via `./run_hosted.sh erdos <name>`, which steps through the token word over SIXTEEN_3 and communicates the verdict
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Lean environment with Mathlib imports and the crystalline versioned store, holding Props, axioms, and evaluated constants
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Lake build system with module dependency resolution, ordering compilation of Lean files and their downstream dependencies

phase_6.cycle_cost: logical inference steps, memory allocations, and CPU cycles during Lean evaluation
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the operation is logically reversible: the mapping from the set of all sufficiency tests to the minimum sufficient N is a deterministic function that can be inverted by retaining the full test results, so no information is irreversibly lost in the abstract domain.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: the Ramsey number is determined and permanently stored; every tested N now has a known sufficiency status
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: the Ramsey number is unknown; the set of all candidate integers has no sufficiency assignments
